params.body:
## Why

The showroom slide is a screen hanging in a dealer's showroom. In September it was redesigned into a fluid Tailwind layout (PR 242): rounded corners everywhere, the dealer logo shrunk to a small mark, the price moved into a rounded white box beside the specs and the badges became rounded pills on a row of their own. Shane held the old screens next to it and wants the original design back.

So the original wins here. The markup and the scss partial come back verbatim from `cutover-baseline`, and the three changes that were behaviour rather than design are re-applied on top.

## What was reverted

- `resources/views/ownstock/showroom_vehicle.blade.php` is the `cutover-baseline` file again: the Bootstrap grid, `.showroom-header`, `.showroom-specs`, `.fixed-blok` with `garantie-blok` / `price-blok` / `stripe-blok`, and the `white_blok.png` and `stripes.png` backgrounds that make the skewed white blocks.
- `resources/sass/settings/_showroom_carousel.scss` is restored (288 lines, unchanged) and its `@import` is back in `resources/sass/app.scss`, in the position it had.
- The `ui-showroom-*` block in `resources/css/refresh.css` is removed with it (55 lines). `StylesheetSyntaxTest` requires every defined `ui-` class to be used and every used one to be defined, so the rules and the classes go together.
- Result at 1920x1080: uppercase make and model top left, dealer name and address top right in small text with the large logo beside them, the photo left on the dark striped ground, year / fuel / mileage in big rows with icons on the right, and the bottom bar of skewed white blocks carrying (right to left) the stripes, the price, the warranty block and the lease block. **No rounded corners anywhere.**

One correction to the brief: in the original the main photo sits directly on the striped background, not on a white panel. The white `single_image.jpg` panel in the old code belonged to the two small thumbnails, and that block was dead (`1 == 2`) and stays removed. The restored file is byte-identical to the baseline apart from the four points below, so this is the original as it was.

## What was kept, and why

| Kept | Why |
|---|---|
| `img.showroom_image[data-src]`, promoted by the carousel script, with `eager` on the single-vehicle screenshot page | PR 244: 60 slides no longer fetch 60 photos at once, and "Download showroom" keeps its photo |
| `VehicleImageService::urlVoor($photo, 'md')` plus the `default_vehicle.png` fallback | a showroom screen does not need the full original file |
| the dead thumbnail block removed, `$images_field` gone, the constrained `primary_photo` relation | it removed one photo query per slide (670 on staging) |
| `CustomerModePrice::showroomPrice(...)` exactly as it stands on `origin/main` | the customer-price unification (PR 304) landed while this branch was open; this branch was rebased on it and takes the call verbatim, only correcting the comment above it (X-74 is fixed there, so the old "margin twice" note would have been false) |
| the warranty conditions (`warrantyEnabled && RealGarantValid`, `Custom::extendedWarranty`) | unchanged |

**Nothing was kept fluid.** The original is not purely fixed-pixel: the title is `6vw`, the photo `52vh`, the header padding `vh`, and those scale on their own. What stays fixed is the bottom bar (120px tall, blocks of 360 and 400px) and the spec rows (50px). At 1366x768 that means the mileage breaks over two lines and the dealer address wraps per word; at 3840x2160 the bottom bar and the specs stay small while the title grows. That is how the original behaved, and rather than smuggle half a redesign back in under the name "fluidity", it is left as it was: where in doubt, the original wins. Say the word if a 4K or a portrait screen is actually in use somewhere and it can be treated as its own question.

## Behaviour change: the lease block (X-75)

The `auto lease` block was forced on for every vehicle by a trailing always-true or-branch. It now follows the real condition:

```php
@if($vehicle?->flexlease_possible && $dealer->show_lease)
```

- `$dealer->show_lease` is a column on `dealers` (tinyint, default 0), set by the switch "leasing tonen" on the dealer form. Absent or 0 means no block.
- `$vehicle->flexlease_possible` is `Vehicle::getFlexleasePossibleAttribute()`: weight known, first registration date known, `VATNeeded == 1`, less than four years since first registration, and mileage at most 50.000 km. Any one of those missing means no block.

**A dealer who does not offer leasing now sees one white block fewer on every slide.** That is what the screen visibly loses, and it is what the client asked for.

## Rules and tests

| Rule | What it says | Soort | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| R S2-7.7 (rewritten) | the lease block appears only when the dealer leases and the vehicle meets the FlexLease conditions | logica | `ShowroomBadgesTest::the_lease_block_appears_only_when_the_dealer_leases_and_the_vehicle_qualifies` (all four combinations) and `::every_missing_flexlease_condition_hides_the_lease_block` (each condition separately) |
| R S2-7.3 (existing) | the extra-warranty block needs the dealer's RealGarant connection and a qualifying vehicle | logica | `ShowroomBadgesTest::the_extra_warranty_block_needs_the_realgarant_connection_and_a_qualifying_vehicle` |
| R S2-7.12 (new) | the warranty block has two forms: months, or "garantie tot date or km" | logica | `ShowroomBadgesTest::the_warranty_block_shows_the_months_or_the_date_and_mileage_form` |
| R S2-7.13 (new) | no warranty filled in still prints twelve months | logica | `ShowroomBadgesTest::a_vehicle_without_a_warranty_shows_twelve_months` |
| R S2-7.14 (new) | the make-up of the slide: which field stands where and where it comes from, skewed white blocks, no rounded corners | scherm | layout, so not testable coverage |

X-75 moved to the resolved table with the reason. `bin/rules-coverage --write` and `bin/rules-page` regenerated `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html`: 683 rules, 88 with a test, of which 81 confirmed by the client. The pricing rules in the same chapter (R S2-7.6, X-74) are the other branch's and were kept exactly as `main` has them; the rebase conflict there was resolved in their favour.

The tests bite: putting the always-true or-branch back makes two of them fail.

## Screenshots

Rendered against a local database with three showroom vehicles (45.000 km, 82.000 km, 12.000 km), the carousel held on the first slide. The photo and the dealer logo are placeholders; the bucket is not reachable from here.

- `showroom-restore-after-1920.png` — the original design: uppercase title top left, dealer and logo top right, photo left, specs right, and the skewed white bottom bar with `27.950 €`, `12 MAANDEN GARANTIE` and `AUTO LEASE / OPTIE`. This is the design Shane compared against.
- `showroom-restore-after-1366.png` — the same slide, wrapping as the original did: the mileage over two lines, the address per word.
- `showroom-restore-after-3840.png` — title and photo scale, the bottom bar and the specs keep their pixel sizes.
- The second slide (82.000 km) carries no lease block, because that vehicle does not meet the FlexLease conditions. The old code would have shown one.

## Checked

- `php artisan view:cache` with a throwaway key, then `php -l` over every compiled view: clean.
- `npm run build`: green. `public/build` is untracked and not committed.
- `php artisan test --filter='Showroom|SmokeTest|StylesheetSyntaxTest|UiApiUsageTest|ClassReferencesResolveTest|BuildContract|CustomerModePrice'`: 158 tests, 982 assertions, green after the rebase, on a throwaway database loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations as CI does, dropped afterwards.
- `bin/rules-coverage` exits 0: every `@rule` tag resolves to a rule that exists.
params.title: Showroom slide: back to the original design
